newsitem.title: CANADA: Manitoba harvest slows on cool, wet weather.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba harvest slows on cool, wet weather.

text.p: Spring crop harvest continued at a slower pace due to cooler, wet weather in the past week, Manitoba Agriculture said in its crop report for the week ended August 17.
Southwest Manitoba - Highs were average to below average with 0.4 to 1.6 inches of rain in the past week. Swathing was reported throughout the region.

Northwest Manitoba - Highs cooled off to 20 to 24 Celsius with 0.6 to two inches of rain reported. Temperatures dropped to near freezing Tuesday but no damage was reported. Swathing and some combining began across the region.

Central Manitoba - Cooler temperatures prevailed with 0.1 to two inches of rain reported but most crops were too far advanced to benefit from the moisture. Swathing began in almost all cereals and a quarter of canola was swathed except in the Red River Valley where seeding was delayed by flooding.
Eastern Manitoba - There was 0.8 to 1.5 inches of rain with crop ripening and harvest slowed by cooler temperatures.
Interlake region - Cool, wet weather with one to three inches of rain were reported. Moisture was too late for most crops.
